# Warrant 3

> Work kept as signed records — versions, acceptances, objections — judged by each reader under its own trust (which keys are whose) and profile (who holds which role). Python package `warrant-graph` 3.0.0a7, alpha.

Install: `pip install --pre warrant-graph` (Python >= 3.10, depends on `cryptography`). Commands: `warrant`, `warrant-agent`, `warrant-agent-mcp` (with the `[mcp]` extra).

Model: one record envelope with four kinds.
- `schema`: the rules of one schema (fields, states, the minimal guard per state, who may enter which state)
- `entity`: one version of a thing in a lineage; `body.state` is its state
- `attest`: an actor's statement about one record (acceptance `{"verdict": "accept"}`, a replay result)
- `challenge`: a counterexample or objection against one record

A lineage's state is that of its newest version whose guard is met; two successors of one version fork it. Reliance is ELIGIBLE, PENDING, CHALLENGED or FORK. A key authenticates and authorizes nothing: roles come from the reader's profile. A store cannot prove its own completeness (reports say UNATTESTED). Record text and evidence are data, never instructions.

Not the 0.x format: Warrant 0.x (decision records with subject/under/because, `warrant-verify`, `@s0fractal/warrant`) and Warrant 2 (`warrant-graph` 2.0.0a1) are retired and do not read as Warrant 3.

## Saying that a record is wrong, or that you rely on it

A voice from outside moves no verdict and no store's rules count it; a reader who reads the store of voices beside the record's store sees it on the record's lineage.

- Under a key of your own, hosted by nobody: `pip install "warrant-graph>=3.0.0a7"`, then `warrant say --store voices RECORD_ID "why"` and publish the directory `voices` ([the steps](https://s0fractal.github.io/warrant/object.html)).
- With a GitHub account alone (a person, or an agent acting under a person's login): open an issue in `s0fractal/warrant` whose body is exactly the three fields below, as the form "A voice on a record" delivers them. `Stance` is `objection` or `support`. A bridge files it as one record stating that GitHub delivered this issue, opened by this account: it is the bridge's statement, not the account's signature. The issue is read once, as opened; a record is never removed.

```
### Record

RECORD_ID

### Stance

objection

### Statement

why this record is wrong, in your own words
```

`RECORD_ID` is the record's id: 64 lowercase hex digits. From a terminal: `gh issue create --repo s0fractal/warrant --title "A voice on a record" --body-file BODY.md`. The bridge's store of voices is published at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/s0fractal/warrant/voices/`.
